title: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry: Axioms and Postulates
seo_title: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry Class 9 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)
standard_code: Class 9, Chapter 5: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry
standard_text: History: geometry in India and Euclid's geometry; Euclid's method of formalising observed phenomena into rigorous mathematics with definitions, common notions, axioms and postulates and theorems; the five postulates of Euclid; showing the relationship between axiom and theorem (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 9 Introduction to Euclid's Geometry worksheet (NCERT Chapter 5): definitions, undefined terms, Euclid's axioms and postulates, using the axioms and true-or-false reasoning. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Axioms and postulates are assumed; theorems are proved
key_sub: Through two distinct points there is exactly one line.
body_html:
How it works

Euclid (about 300 BCE) collected geometry in his Elements. He started from definitions, axioms (common notions used in all mathematics) and postulates (assumptions about geometry), and proved theorems from them.

Axioms include: things equal to the same thing are equal; equals added to equals give equals; the whole is greater than the part.

Postulates: a line can be drawn through any two points; a segment can be extended; a circle can be drawn with any centre and radius; all right angles are equal; the fifth postulate is about parallel lines.

Example

If AC = BD and C, D lie on AB as A, C, D, B, show AD = CB.

AC + CD = BD + CD (Axiom 2)

So AD = CB

Answer: AD = CB

Example

How many lines pass through two points A and B?

Axiom 5.1: a unique line

Answer: Exactly one

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up axioms and postulates. Postulates are about geometry only.
  • Thinking many lines can pass through two points. Only one can.
  • Calling a proved result a postulate. Proved results are theorems.

faq.q: What is the difference between an axiom and a postulate?
faq.a: Euclid used axioms (common notions) for assumptions used throughout mathematics, and postulates for assumptions specific to geometry. Today both words are often used for any basic assumption.

1) A straight line can be drawn between any two points. 2) A segment can be produced indefinitely. 3) A circle can be drawn with any centre and radius. 4) All right angles are equal. 5) The parallel postulate.

faq.q: Why are point, line and plane undefined?
faq.a: Defining them needs other words (part, breadth, length) that would also need defining, so they are taken as undefined terms.
For every line l and every point P not on l, there is exactly one line through P parallel to l. It is equivalent to Euclid's fifth postulate.

items.q: AB = CD = 27 cm. A length of 17 cm is added to each. Which statement is correct?
c: The new lengths are equal (44 cm each), by Axiom 3
The new lengths are equal (44 cm each), by Axiom 2
The new lengths are equal (459 cm each), by Axiom 2
The new lengths are 44 cm and 27 cm
items.e: Equals added to equals give equal wholes (Axiom 2): 44 cm each.

items.q: C is the mid-point of AB and AB = 36 cm. Find AC.
items.e: AC = CB and AC + CB = AB, so 2AC = AB and AC = 18 cm.

items.q: C is the mid-point of AB and AB = 8 cm. Find AC.
items.e: AC = CB and AC + CB = AB, so 2AC = AB and AC = 4 cm.

items.q: Point C lies between A and B. AC = 8 cm and CB = 14 cm. Find AB.
items.e: C is between A and B, so AB = AC + CB = 22 cm.

items.q: Point C lies between A and B. AB = 24 cm and AC = 9 cm. Find CB.
items.e: AC + CB = AB, so CB = 24 − 9 = 15 cm.

items.q: On a line the points are in the order A, B, C, D with AC = BD. If AB = 6 cm, find CD.
items.e: AC = AB + BC and BD = BC + CD. Subtracting BC from equals (Axiom 3) gives AB = CD = 6 cm.

items.q: C is the mid-point of AB and AB = 20 cm. Find AC.
items.e: AC = CB and AC + CB = AB, so 2AC = AB and AC = 10 cm.

items.e: C is between A and B, so AB = AC + CB = 15 cm.

items.q: Point C lies between A and B. AB = 16 cm and AC = 7 cm. Find CB.
items.e: AC + CB = AB, so CB = 16 − 7 = 9 cm.

items.e: AC = CB and AC + CB = AB, so 2AC = AB and AC = 20 cm.

items.e: AC = CB and AC + CB = AB, so 2AC = AB and AC = 23 cm.

items.e: AC = AB + BC and BD = BC + CD. Subtracting BC from equals (Axiom 3) gives AB = CD = 11 cm.

items.q: Point C lies between A and B. AB = 15 cm and AC = 3 cm. Find CB.

items.q: C is the mid-point of AB and AB = 6 cm. Find AC.

items.e: AC = CB and AC + CB = AB, so 2AC = AB and AC = 12 cm.

items.q: Point C lies between A and B. AB = 16 cm and AC = 9 cm. Find CB.
items.e: AC + CB = AB, so CB = 16 − 9 = 7 cm.

items.q: Point C lies between A and B. AB = 13 cm and AC = 2 cm. Find CB.

items.q: True or false? A terminated line can be produced indefinitely on both sides.
items.e: True. This is Euclid's second postulate.

items.q: True or false? Every point of a line segment AB, except A and B, lies between A and B.
items.e: True. That is what “between” means for a segment.

items.q: True or false? Two distinct intersecting lines can both be parallel to the same line.
items.e: False. This contradicts an equivalent form of the fifth postulate.

items.q: True or false? A line segment has a definite length.
items.e: True. It has two end points and a fixed length.

items.q: True or false? A circle can be drawn with any point as centre and any length as radius.
items.e: True. This is Euclid's third postulate.

items.q: True or false? A ray can be measured with a ruler.
items.e: False. A ray goes on forever in one direction, so it has no length.

items.q: True or false? If x + y = 10 and x = z, then z + y = 10.
items.e: True. Replacing x by the equal thing z keeps the sum equal (Axiom 1 with Axiom 2).

items.q: True or false? Through a point not on a line, more than one parallel to that line can be drawn.
items.e: False. Playfair's axiom: exactly one parallel can be drawn.

items.q: True or false? If AB = PQ and PQ = XY, then AB = XY.
items.e: True. Things equal to the same thing are equal to one another (Axiom 1).

items.q: True or false? All right angles are equal to one another.
items.e: True. This is Euclid's fourth postulate.

items.q: True or false? Two lines in a plane always meet at a point.
items.e: False. Parallel lines never meet.

items.q: True or false? A theorem is a statement that is proved.
items.e: True. Theorems are proved from definitions, axioms and earlier results.

items.q: True or false? Euclid's fifth postulate is about circles.
items.e: False. It is about parallel lines.

items.q: True or false? The edges of a surface are curves only.
items.e: False. Euclid said the edges of a surface are lines.

items.q: True or false? Only one line can pass through a single point.
items.e: False. Infinitely many lines pass through one point.

items.q: True or false? If two circles are equal, then their radii are equal.
items.e: True. Equal circles coincide when placed on each other, so their radii are equal.

items.q: True or false? Things which are halves of the same things are equal to one another.
items.e: True. This is Euclid's seventh axiom.

items.q: True or false? There are infinitely many lines that pass through two distinct points.
items.e: False. Exactly one line passes through two distinct points.

items.q: True or false? The part can be greater than the whole.
items.e: False. Axiom 5: the whole is greater than the part.

items.q: True or false? Euclid's definitions of point and line are now accepted as precise.
items.e: False. Words like “part” and “breadth” need further definition, so point and line are taken as undefined.
